title: Rolling Hit Counter
statement:
Design a counter that records event timestamps and reports how many landed inside the latest 300-second rolling window.

Contract
- Create a new `Solution` with an empty history and a fixed 300-second window.
- `hit(timestamp)` records one event at that integer timestamp. Calls are made with nondecreasing timestamps, and multiple hits at the same timestamp are distinct.
- `hitsInLastWindow(timestamp)` returns the number of recorded hits with time strictly greater than `timestamp - 300` and less than or equal to `timestamp`. Older hits may be discarded.
- Timestamps are non-negative `int` values.

Examples
`hit(1), hit(2), hit(300), hitsInLastWindow(300)` => `3`
`hit(1), hit(301), hitsInLastWindow(301)` => `1`
`hit(5), hit(5), hit(304), hitsInLastWindow(304)` => `3`
hints: Keep every timestamp in a queue before optimizing.
When a query or hit arrives, remove timestamps at or before `current - 300`.

Compress equal timestamps into `(time, count)` entries so repeated hits do not require repeated cleanup work. Intended complexity: O(1) amortized time per operation and O(1) space because the window is fixed at 300 seconds.
inputSyntax: Input: semicolon-separated operations hit <time> and count <time>, for example: hit 1; hit 2; hit 300; count 300
